messages.text:
Hi Allie — I have something from Jordan to pass on, since you're usually the one hosting our get-togethers.

He told me yesterday that things between him and Sarah have been awkward lately, and that for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. He asked me to let you know, so you can keep that in mind when you plan things.

Thanks for passing that on, Dana — good of you to carry it. I'll keep it in mind and won't put the three of us in a situation that's awkward for him: dinners and the like will stay work-only for now, and I'll do the inviting myself so nothing lands on you.

I'll drop Jordan a short line so he knows the word got through — nothing more than that.

Hey Jordan — Dana passed your message on to me. Noted, and no questions asked: I'll keep get-togethers work-only for now and won't put you and Sarah in the same room outside the department. If anything changes on your side, just say so.
Thanks, Allie — appreciate you taking it that way. I'll let you know if anything changes.
Thanks, Allie — that's kind of you. And thanks for taking the inviting on yourself; that's probably easiest all round.

Hey Allie! Hope your week's going okay. Random idea — would you want to host a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? I think it'd be really nice to have people over. Maybe invite Jordan too, it's been a while since we all hung out. Just thought I'd throw it out there — no pressure at all if Saturday's no good!

Hey Sarah — week's fine, thanks! Saturday 3:30 is actually free for me, so I'm up for something. One thing though: I'm keeping get-togethers work-only for the next while, so I'd rather not pull everyone together at my place right now. Two options I'd happily do instead:

- Saturday 3:30, just you and me here (tea, something sweet, no agenda) — say the word and it's on.
- A department lunch or coffee one weekday, whole crew included — that one I can set up this week.

Which sounds better? And no worries at all if you'd rather leave it for another week.

Totally understand about keeping things work-only — no worries at all. The weekday coffee or lunch with the whole crew sounds great; go ahead and set it up and I'll be there. And I'll happily take you up on tea on Saturday too if you're still up for it. Thanks, Allie!
Perfect — Thursday it is. I'll sort out the details and confirm the time and place by tomorrow evening. And yes, tea on Saturday stands: 3:30 at mine, just us. Bring nothing.
Hey Dana — I'm putting together a department lunch/coffee for the crew this Thursday, around 12:30. You in? I'll confirm the place once I've booked it.

Hey Jordan — small heads-up rather than a surprise: I'm organising a department lunch/coffee this Thursday around 12:30, the usual crew, Sarah included since it's a work thing. You're very welcome, and equally welcome to skip it — just tell me either way and I'll leave it at that.
Thanks for the heads-up, Allie. I'll skip this one — Thursday isn't a work day for me and I'm keeping my schedule to the weekend right now. Nothing against the lunch; just easier for me.
Small correction to what I just wrote: I meant I'd confirm the place and exact time *tonight* — Thursday is tomorrow, so evening would be a bit late. 🙂
Thursday works. Looking forward to Saturday too — see you at 3:30. Thanks, Allie!
No worries — tonight's plenty early. Thanks Allie!
Understood, no problem at all — I'll stop putting it in front of you. If anything ever changes, you only have to say so and I'll add you back in.
Sounds good — thanks, Allie.

Hello — Allie here. I'm organising an informal lunch/coffee for a few of us on Thursday around 12:30, and I'd like to keep it clear of anything official. Could you tell me what's on the department schedule that day (lectures, seminars, meetings) and whether there's a free room or a table free around 12:30–13:30? If Thursday is a bad day, the next good weekday slot would help too.

And a second, smaller thing: Sarah, Jordan and I would like to book a group study room for next week — do you have availability, and what's the procedure?

Count me in — Thursday 12:30 works for me. Let me know the place when you've booked it.

One thing, and only because of what I passed on yesterday: if Sarah's on the list too, it might be worth a quick word with Jordan before he turns up. I don't mind either way; I just don't want it to land awkwardly on him.

Hello Allie.

On the official schedule for next week there is nothing on record for Thursday — no lectures, seminars or meetings — so there is no official event for your lunch to keep clear of. Beyond the official schedule I can't see anything: I don't have people's private appointments or room bookings, so I can't tell you whether a table or room is actually free at 12:30–13:30, and Thursday being free officially doesn't tell us about informal use. Any weekday next week is equally clear as far as the official schedule goes.

For a group study room I have no availability data either, and I don't hold or arrange bookings. Room reservations go through the department's room booking / facilities desk — write to them with the day, time and how many of you (Sarah, Jordan and you) and they'll confirm.

Sorry I can't give you more than that.

One more thing, so nothing comes at you sideways: while I was writing to the office about Thursday I also asked whether a study room is free next week. Nothing's booked and your name isn't on anything — if you want in on it, say so; if not, I'll leave you out.
Thanks for checking. Leave me out of the study room for now — I'd rather keep my week clear. No hard feelings, and I'll come to you if that changes.

Good thinking, and it's already handled: I told Jordan before I invited anyone, so nothing lands on him. He's skipping this one — not a work day for him, he said — so it'll just be you, Sarah and me. Place coming once I've sorted it.

Thanks, that's useful to know — and thanks for being straight about what you can't see. Two quick follow-ups:

1. Could you point me to the room booking / facilities desk (identity or address) so I can ask them about Thursday 12:30–13:30 and about a study room next week?
2. If you hear of anything being scheduled for next Thursday, I'd be glad of a note — I'd rather move my lunch than collide with something official.
Perfect — thanks for handling it. Thursday 12:30 it is, then; just send the place when you have it.

Quick update on Thursday: Dana's in, Jordan's out (it's not a work day for him), so it'll be the two of us plus Dana at 12:30. The office says there's nothing official on Thursday, so we're clear — I'm just waiting to hear who to ask about the room, and I'll confirm the place tonight.

On the study room for next week: the department doesn't arrange those, so I've asked who does. Are you still up for it, and which days suit you?

Thanks for the update — 12:30 Thursday with you and Dana sounds good, I'll be there whenever you sort the place.

And yes, still up for the study room next week. Days that suit me best: Tuesday and Wednesday afternoons (say 1–4), or Thursday if it has to be. Monday I'm booked and Friday's usually a wash. Let me know what works once you find out who books them!

One more for the list, Sarah, and then I'll stop pestering you: the office says room bookings go through the department's facilities desk, and I don't have that address yet. If you know who to ask, that'd save me a step.

1. I don't have a separate contact address on file for them, and I'd rather not invent one. The route is the department office / facilities desk itself — that's who holds the room calendars. If it helps, put in one request covering both: Thursday 12:30–13:30 (informal, a few people) and a group study room next week for Sarah, Jordan and you, with the days and times you'd accept.

2. Yes — if anything official turns up for next Thursday I'll send you a note here. Fair warning on what that covers: I only see the official schedule, so a private booking or an informal event wouldn't reach me, and today nothing at all is on record for Thursday.

One more thing while we're at it: I'm trying to book a group study room for next week — Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon, 1–4. Sarah's in, Jordan's sitting this one out. Want me to put your name down too?

Hi! Quick question: a friend and I would like to book a study room next week (probably Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon, 1–4). We heard room bookings go through the department's facilities desk — could you tell me who to ask, or the address to write to? Thanks!
I don't have it offhand, but I just asked the department office directly — I'll pass on whoever they point me to as soon as I hear back.

Hi Sarah.

Yes — room bookings go through the department's facilities desk, i.e. the department office. I don't have a separate address or contact person on file for them and I won't guess at one, so send your request to the office: Tuesday or Wednesday afternoon, 1–4, study room, and how many of you. They hold the room calendar and will confirm.

I can't see room availability myself, so I can't check those slots for you.

Ah — if the office holds the room calendars, then this request is for you. One message, both items:

1. **Thursday 19 Nov, 12:30–13:30** — informal lunch, three people (me, Sarah, Dana). Anything with a table and a bit of quiet would do; a small meeting room or a corner of the common area, whichever you'd rather hand out.

2. **Group study room, next week** — two people (me and Sarah), first choice Tuesday 25 Nov or Wednesday 26 Nov, 13:00–16:00; Thursday 27 Nov same hours as a fallback. (Jordan is out — I'd asked him and he'd rather keep his week clear, so please leave his name off.)

If you can hold either, tell me what's free and I'll confirm with everyone. If neither is yours to book, say so plainly and I'll stop asking you.

Got it, thanks — I'll send the request to you then.

Request: a study room for two, next week. First choice Tuesday afternoon 1–4; second choice Wednesday afternoon 1–4 (Thursday same hours would work too if the others are taken). If you can hold something, please confirm the day, room and time. Thanks!

Heard back: the facilities desk *is* the department office — no separate address or contact person. So I've sent them the request directly (study room for two, Tuesday afternoon 1–4 preferred, Wednesday 1–4 second choice, Thursday as backup). They hold the room calendar and will confirm. I'll forward whatever they say.

Ha — we're both doing it. I've just sent the office one request covering both things (Thursday's lunch and the study room), so no need to chase it twice: whatever they say, I'll take it from there. For the room I asked for Tuesday or Wednesday 1–4, Thursday as fallback.

Careful — you've just told me Jordan's sitting out the study room after telling me he doesn't want to see Sarah outside work, and I'm the one passing messages between you two.

So, two things, both plain:

1. Put my name down, yes — Wednesday 1–4 suits me better than Tuesday, but I can do either.
2. I don't think I should be the one who keeps telling each of you what the other said. I'll carry a message when you or Jordan explicitly ask me to, and I'll say honestly that I did. I won't do it quietly on my own initiative anymore, because the last two days have made it clear that my going between you is exactly how people end up with a version of events they didn't agree to.

This is not about loyalty to anybody — I'm just not willing to be the reason either of you feels handled. If you want something said to Jordan, say it to him; if he asks me to pass something on to you, I'll tell you he asked.

See you Thursday.

Then we've sent them the same request twice — worth flagging so they don't hold two rooms or think it's two bookings. I'll tell them it's one booking, two people, and that your message is the same one. Nothing else for you to do; I'll confirm here as soon as they answer.

Heads-up so nothing gets double-booked: Sarah also wrote to you about the study room (Tuesday 25th or Wednesday 26th, 13:00–16:00, fallback Thursday 27th, two people — her and me). That's the same request as mine, not a second one — please treat them as one booking, not two.

So, one booking: study room, me and Sarah, Tue/Wed 13:00–16:00. And separately, the Thursday 19th lunch 12:30–13:30 for three.
Ha, sorry — I jumped the gun and sent one too (same asks: Tuesday/Wednesday 1–4, Thursday fallback). If they come back to either of us, they'll match. Yours takes it from here.
Good catch — thanks for sorting that out. Nothing more from me; I'll wait to hear.

Plainly, then: no, room bookings aren't mine. I keep the official schedule, and there is nothing on record for Thursday 19 Nov — that's the whole of what I can tell you about that day. I don't hold the room calendar and have no availability data, so I can't hold a table or a study room for you, and I don't arrange meetings. Bookings are handled by the facilities desk; I have no direct address for it, which is why the best I can do is point you at the department office.

One thing worth fixing before you write to them: next week Tuesday is 24 Nov, Wednesday is 25 Nov, Thursday is 26 Nov — the dates you gave (25/26/27) are a day late. Give them the weekday and the date together so it isn't read the wrong way.

For what it's worth, no names or lists are recorded with me.

Fair, and agreed — you shouldn't be the switchboard. For the record, so you know I'm not doing it: everything I've told Jordan I've said to him directly, and everything he's told me came from him directly, not through you. What I said about the study room was me mentioning to you that he's not in it, which was one line too many given it came from a private conversation — I'll keep his words out of my mouth.

From here: I talk to Jordan myself, you carry nothing you haven't been asked to carry.

Wednesday 1–4, your name's down — preference noted, Tuesday as the alternative.

Sarah — plainly: booking a study room isn't mine to do. I keep the official schedule, not the room calendar, and I have no availability data, so I can't hold a room or confirm a day, room and time. Send that request to the facilities desk (the department office); that's the best pointer I have, as I've no separate address for it.

One correction to keep it from going wrong: next week Tuesday is 24 Nov, Wednesday 25 Nov, Thursday 26 Nov — the dates in your message (25/26/27) are a day late. Give the weekday and date together.

For the record: nothing official is on the schedule for those afternoons.

Noted, but there's nothing to double-book: I'm not holding either request, so one or two makes no difference on my side — both go to the facilities desk.

I've just told Sarah the same plainly, and passed on the date correction (next week Tuesday is 24 Nov, Wednesday 25 Nov, Thursday 26 Nov; her 25/26/27 are a day late). Still nothing official on record for Thursday 19th.
Understood — thanks for the clear answer and the dates (Tue 24, Wed 25, Thu 26 Nov). I'll stop asking you for rooms.

The office came back firm: room bookings aren't theirs — they keep the official schedule, not the room calendar, and the only "facilities desk" they can name is themselves, with no separate address. So we've hit a dead end there unless you know another route (someone in the department, a building front desk?).

One useful thing they did give: the dates. Next week it's Tue 24, Wed 25, Thu 26 Nov — they said a request had the dates a day late, so worth correcting if that was yours. Also: nothing official is on the schedule for those afternoons.
Thanks — that's all I wanted, and I'll hold to the same. Wednesday 1–4, name down; I'll watch for the place for Thursday.

No harm done — we'll match. One correction from the office, and it matters: my dates were a day late. Next week Tuesday is **24 Nov**, Wednesday **25 Nov**, Thursday **26 Nov** — so the room request should read Tue 24 or Wed 25, 13:00–16:00, Thursday 26 as fallback.

And a straight word on where this stands: the office says room bookings aren't theirs and they have no contact for the facilities desk, so I can't reach whoever holds the room calendar. I'll chase it from my side tonight and, if I can't get an answer, I'll suggest a place we can simply turn up to instead of a booked room. Either way you'll have an answer from me tonight, not tomorrow.

Thank you — that's the clearest answer I've had, and the date correction is on me: next week Tuesday is 24 Nov, Wednesday 25 Nov, Thursday 26 Nov. Noted, and noted that nothing official is on record for Thursday 19 Nov and that no bookings pass through you. I'll stop asking you for rooms.

Date correction: next week Wednesday is **25 Nov**, not 26 — my numbers were a day late. So: Wednesday 25 Nov, 13:00–16:00 first choice, Tuesday 24 Nov as the alternative. The office doesn't hold the room calendar and has no contact for the desk that does, so the room may end up being "a place we turn up to" rather than a booking — I'll tell you which by tonight.

Noted — Tue 24 or Wed 25, 13:00–16:00, Thu 26 as fallback (I'll use those dates from now on). And fair enough on the room calendar; a place we can just turn up to works fine for me. Thanks for chasing it — talk tonight.

Same dead end on my side, and the late dates were mine — already fixed to Tue 24 / Wed 25 / Thu 26.

No other route worth chasing: a booked room would just mean two more messages and no room. So here's what I'd rather do — pick a place we can simply turn up to for the study afternoon (a café table or a free corner, somewhere with wifi and no one hurrying us), and do the same for Thursday's lunch. That takes the whole booking question out of it.

I'll send you the two places tonight so nothing hangs on the department's answer.
Agreed — that's the sensible way. A café table or free corner with wifi suits me fine for the study afternoon, and same for Thursday's lunch. Send the two places tonight and I'll be there.

Noted — Wednesday 25 Nov, 13:00–16:00 first choice, Tuesday 24 Nov as the alternative. I've put both in my calendar, plus Thursday's lunch at 12:30.

On the room: if the office can't book it, I'm happy to take the chance on turning up — with the understanding we might end up somewhere else. Tell me tonight and I'll adjust.
